claim: The axioms of `ConvexSpace` (`assoc`, `single`, `ext`) do not imply idempotence, so the class admits instances that are not convex spaces, and `proof_wanted convexCombo₂_same` is false in general and can never be proved. Counter-model: R = M = ℝ with `convexCombination f xs := ∑ i ∈ f.support, f i * xs i + H f`, where `H f = -∑ f i * log (f i)` is Shannon entropy. `single` holds because H of a point mass is 0; `ext` holds because nothing depends on xs off the support; `assoc` holds by the entropy chain rule H (f.comp g) = H f + ∑ k, f k * H (g k). Yet `convexCombo₂ (1/2) (1/2) _ _ _ x x = x + log 2 ≠ x`. (The same works over ℚ with F(q) = q * padicValRat 2 q in place of q log q.) What is missing is naturality in the index type: `convexCombination` depends on the indexing and not only on the pushed-forward distribution on M.
requested_change: Replace the `ext` field with a naturality axiom: for `e : ι → ι'`, `convexCombination (f.map e) xs = convexCombination f (xs ∘ e)`, with `FiniteProbability.map` defined via `Finsupp.mapDomain`. This axiom implies `ext` (restrict to the support subtype) and idempotence (map to `Unit`, then `single`), which also settles the TODO on whether `ext` is needed. Alternatively, make `convexCombination` take a `FiniteProbability R M`, i.e. an algebra for the finitely supported distribution monad. Also delete the inline `-- Perhaps this follows from assoc` comment.
evidence: Read from the diff: the class has exactly the three fields `assoc`, `single` and `ext`, and `ext` only lets `xs` vary for a fixed `f`. No field relates combinations over different index types, and the entropy chain rule satisfies `assoc` exactly as `FiniteProbability.comp` is defined (weights f k * g k i on ⟨k, i⟩). This is a pen-and-paper counter-model, not machine-checked; building it in-file would need Real.log imports. zulip_search found no prior discussion of these axioms.

claim: The `total` proof of `FiniteProbability.comp` is a 25-line machine-generated proof ("minimally cleaned up from a proof by Aristotle"). It restates `f` as `f.sum single`, uses three intermediate `have`s, and closes with `convert … using 1`, `simp_all` and `aesop`. It is only `Finsupp.sum_sum_index` followed by the fact that each inner sum equals its outer weight.
requested_change:
Replace the `total` proof with:
    have hg (m : κ) (r : R) : (r • (g m).weights).sum (fun _ r => r) = r := by
      have := (g m).total
      rw [Finsupp.sum] at this
      rw [Finsupp.sum_of_support_subset _ Finsupp.support_smul _ (fun _ _ => rfl)]
      simp only [Finsupp.coe_smul, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, ← Finset.mul_sum, this, mul_one]
    rw [Finsupp.sum_sum_index (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ _ _ => rfl)]
    simp only [Finsupp.sum_embDomain, hg]
    exact f.total
and drop the Aristotle comment.
evidence: lean_verify_edit (declaration FiniteProbability.comp) with this `total` proof: success. A first attempt using `Finsupp.sum_smul_index` failed with Unknown constant. declaration_search places that lemma in Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/SMul.lean, which this file does not import, so the proof uses `Finsupp.sum_of_support_subset` and `Finsupp.support_smul` instead.

claim: The field `ConvexSpace.ext` states a congruence property of `convexCombination` (points agreeing on the support give equal combinations), not extensionality of `ConvexSpace` structures. In Mathlib, `Foo.ext` is reserved for extensionality of `Foo` itself (the name an `@[ext]` attribute on the class would generate), so this name is misleading and will collide.
